cards.title: Act Like You Belong
cards.instruction: You do not understand what is happening. Copy the confidence around you and never admit confusion.

cards.title: What Are We Now?
cards.instruction: Find out how someone defines the relationship without directly asking for a label.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: I've ticked the same hotel box as you for your sister's wedding. Shall I ask for a double bed for us?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: I ticked step-free access for Mum. We can share a room to save money, though.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: Of course, access first. Double or twin beds, then?

beats.speaker: B
beats.text: Twins. I've told my sister you're coming with me.

beats.speaker: A
beats.text: When they gather the family for photographs, do I wait beside you or find a seat with the other guests?

cardFidelity.evidence: A1 copies wrong hotel checkbox and probes shared bed; A3 covers access correction then probes twins; A5 tests family inclusion after B4 ambiguous coming-with-me.

responseLogic.evidence: B2 access correction plus room offer supports A3 beds; B4 twins and family report motivate A5 photographs.

relationship.evidence: B2 offers practical saving and B4 gives boundary without gratuitous hostility.

heightening.evidence: A5 changes proxy from bed to family position using B4 sister disclosure.

specificity.evidence: A1 sister wedding/hotel and B2 mother access show all necessary roles.

brevityWit.evidence: A5 concrete photograph choice is a purposeful indirect relationship question.
